topics.title: Howard Discusses Romantic Relationships & Racial Violence
topics.summary: During a lengthy conversation, Howard discusses an incident where a black man was fatally attacked by white youths after dating a neighborhood woman. He repeatedly expresses confusion about women’s behavior during orgasm and makes racially charged remarks regarding relationships between white men and Black individuals, referencing stereotypes and personal anecdotes.

topics.title: Ed, The Salad Maker & A Confused White Guy
topics.summary: A man recounts a brief and bizarre relationship with Ed, a larger-than-life friend who has an unusual hairstyle and a penchant for dating black women. Their time together involved alcohol, embarrassing encounters, and ultimately, the revelation that Ed’s girlfriend was being influenced by her parents' disapproval of white men.

topics.title: Stern Discusses McMillan Family & Pete Rose
topics.summary: Howard Stern discussed the disturbing case of the McMillan family murders while simultaneously covering Pete Rose’s continued insistence he deserves reinstatement to baseball. He highlighted Rose's denial of gambling and expressed disbelief at his claims, alongside details about abuse and child endangerment within the McMillans³ story.

topics.title: Sports, Cocaine & Hypnotized Interns
topics.summary: A man sells sports photographs for seventy-nine dollars while Dale Barra (son of Yogi Berra) is indicted on cocaine charges. Simultaneously, two twin women jump from a Brooklyn building and Howard Stern discusses feeding shrimp to his assistant, alongside arguments about Leona Helmsley’s case and the bizarre behavior of hypnotized interns.

topics.title: Brooklyn Puppy City Hypnosis
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, Howard attempts to hypnotize his intern Jackie at Brooklyn’s ‘Puppy City,’ involving fantasies about sexual attraction and manipulation. The conversation includes references to reciting poetry as a method of control and attempting to influence her behavior.

topics.title: Stern & Associates Debate Lobby Cleanliness
topics.summary: During a radio segment, Howard Stern and his co-hosts discuss the presence of discarded coffee cups and styrofoam in the Wysp morning show’s lobby. They debate whether guests should be expected to clean up after themselves, leading to humorous arguments about responsibilities and potential guest behavior.
